children: Nomura remains positive on the health insurance sector after hosting Joy Chakraborty, Deputy CEO of P D Hinduja National Hospital & Medical Research Centre, on August 28. "Overall, the multiple measures being discussed/undertaken by the industry body and regulator keeps us optimistic," Nomura said, reiterating its 'Buy' ratings on Star Health and Niva Bupa Health.

Chakraborty highlighted "rapid changes in customer behaviour (demand for high-end services, better rooms, etc.) with higher adoption of private insurance". He also shared insights into the five working committees set up by the insurance regulator, with participation from insurance and healthcare industry bodies.

The committees, formed in March 2026, are working towards five key initiatives: "i) categorisation of hospitals (includes common empanelment of hospitals), ii) joint code of conduct, iii) analytical studies, iv) simplified products and wellness, and v) National Health Claim Exchange (NHCX)." Discussions around standard treatment guidelines are also underway, although the committees are still some time away from taking a final decision.

On the hospital-insurer relationship, Chakraborty said "friction between hospitals and health insurers is a global phenomenon". He believes pricing should be approached cautiously as rising healthcare costs lead to higher health insurance premiums, which eventually impact the end customer. At the same time, "the insurance sector has empowered customers /patients in adoption of high-end facilities like better rooms, robotic processes, etc." He believes hospitals and health insurers should work together to keep pricing under control.

Nomura said it had highlighted the "chaotic dynamics of the healthcare ecosystem" in its initiation note, 21st century Mahabharat. The brokerage noted that the need for "standard treatment protocols, transparent pricing, etc." remains under discussion.

"Overall, we believe the measures taken by industry bodies are in the right direction," Nomura said. "Any shift in industry dynamics due to intervention from regulatory bodies is a positive, in our view."

"We continue to like health insurers as measures undertaken by insurers like annual repricing, cohort-based repricing make their loss ratio predictable," Nomura said, reiterating its view that loss ratios for health insurers can be "far more predictable going ahead."

title: Nomura retains 'Buy' on Star Health, Niva Bupa; sees more predictable loss ratios
